topic.title: Dash Line Drawing
topic.description: Draws a dashed line by alternating penup() and pendown() calls inside a loop. Teaches pen control for non-continuous drawing.

learningNotes.whatILearned: A dashed line is just: draw, lift the pen, move, put the pen down, and do it fifty times.
learningNotes.challenges: Nothing in the file says the pen has to be lifted at all, which is the one idea behind a dashed line.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Add one comment on `penup()` — that is the whole trick — and one on the loop bound.

files.description: Draws a dashed line with penup/pendown alternation.

misconceptions: `penup()` lifts the pen so the turtle moves without drawing; `pendown()` puts it back — that is the entire idea behind a dashed line
The dash is half the distance of the gap, which is why the file moves 10, skips 10, rather than some other ratio
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**0 + 30 + 0 = 30%**

**This file cannot be run here.** It needs `tkinter`, and this
machine has no display and no `tkinter` — so the 40 points for *it runs* are
not ones I can give, and they are not given. The other two bands are judged
by reading the code, carefully, line by line.

There is a bigger point here, and it is worth saying plainly: **`tkinter`
does not exist on Termux either.** These files cannot be run on the phone
this whole system is built around. They are not broken — they are stranded.

**What is right, by reading**

It is right. Fifty dashes of ten units with ten-unit gaps between them, the turtle moving forward the whole time, and `turtle.done()` at the end so the window stays open. The ratio is exactly what a dashed line looks like.

**What is not**

No comments, and the file has exactly one idea in it — that a dash is made by drawing, lifting the pen, moving, and putting the pen down. Without a word of explanation the reader has to spot `penup()` and work out what it means.

**The one thing to fix first**

```python
t.penup()  # Lift the pen: the turtle moves here without drawing.
```

One line on the one idea the file has.
